subject: Graceful rollforward plan for third‑party SDK consumers
messages:
From: Tom Mercer <tom.mercer@aegistools.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena@aegistools.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: graceful rollforward support for Aegis SDK consumers

Mina — thanks again for the quick sync yesterday. Following up with a concise ask from our engineering team at Aegis. We integrate Redwood via the Java + Node SDKs and our customers run the SDK in tightly regulated CI/CD pipelines. Two items are blocking our next release: 

1) We need a predictable rollforward path when Redwood introduces minor releases that change request/response shapes (not full breaking semantics, but fields added/renamed).
2) We’d like a lightweight test harness we can run in our CI to detect regressions early (contract tests that validate API/SDK surface).

Concretely, can Redwood provide: 
- A documented "graceful rollforward" policy that defines timelines (deprecation window, opt-in flags, removal) for non-critical shape changes.
- A compatibility test runner (or sample tests) we can execute during our presubmit gates.
- An optional short-term compatibility adapter (single-file) we can include while we migrate.

I’m attaching a short diff that shows the fields we're concerned about and an integration matrix that maps which Aegis customers use which SDK versions. We’d like to align on a plan and a timeline — our customers expect a patch release in Q3 so time is tight.

Attachments: proposal-diff.patch (text), aegis-integration-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

—Tom
Principal Engineer, Integrations
Aegis Tools
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Mercer <tom.mercer@aegistools.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena@aegistools.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: graceful rollforward support for Aegis SDK consumers

Tom — thanks for the clear ask and for the diff + matrix. This is exactly the kind of partner feedback we want to bake into our release process. High level: we can offer a 4–8 week rollforward cadence that combines opt-in runtime flags, a temporary compatibility adapter, and a contract test harness you can run in CI. Proposed next steps below.

Summary proposal (very high level):
- Week 0–1: Discovery & scoping — confirm exact fields and SDK versions (we’ll run a quick matrix match against your attachment).
- Week 2–3: Adapter & flags — we'll create a small adapter package and runtime feature flags for the server to honor legacy shapes (opt-in by header).
- Week 4–6: Contract tests & CI integration — provide the compat-test-runner and a sample suite (GH Actions + Maven/npm examples).
- Week 6–8: Staged rollout & monitoring — canary on Dedicated pools, toggle opt-in off for customers that are ready.

I’ve looped in Marissa from Partner Eng and Jonas from Platform to scope the engineering work. Vanessa will help coordinate required SOW/partner success touchpoints. Can you do a 45-minute joint call Tuesday 2027-06-15 10:00am PT so we can lock timelines and owners? I’ve attached an initial outline to give you something concrete to review.

Attachments: initial-rollforward-outline.md

Thanks — looking forward to working through this.

—Mina Haddad
Sr. Manager, Partner Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Tom Mercer <tom.mercer@aegistools.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: graceful rollforward support for Aegis SDK consumers

Tom / Mina — quick technical note from the runtime side. I sketched a possible minimal approach that should keep risk low and speed up partner adoption: 

- Runtime feature gates: server honors a request header X-RW-Legacy-Shape=v1 which enables a compatibility layer that maps legacy field names to new ones. This is cheap to add and reversible.
- Adapter package: we’ll publish tiny adapter packages for Java/Node (< 100 LOC) that translate inbound/outbound payloads; these are intended to be short-lived.
- Compat test runner: our team already has a prototype (see repo below). We can provide a GH Action and a local script that runs contract tests against staging. The tests will verify schema shape, required fields, and sample flow-based tokens/performance checks.

Risks / constraints: we can do the above as non-breaking server-side features but long-term maintenance for many partner-specific adapters is costly. We should limit supported adapters to two major release windows and push for customers to upgrade their consumers to the new shape.

Next concrete step from my side: I'll create the compat-test-runner repo and a presubmit example by Monday 2027-06-14 and post links. For the call on 2027-06-15, I’ll prepare a short demo of the test runner and a checklist for the staged rollout.

Links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compat-test-runner (prototype)

—Jonas Weber
Platform Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@aegistools.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Mercer <tom.mercer@aegistools.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: graceful rollforward support for Aegis SDK consumers

Mina / Jonas — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear plan. We can do the June 15 call at 10am PT. A few quick notes from Aegis: 

- We’ll run the compat-test-runner in a fork of our CI and share initial failures within 48 hours of receiving the GH Action.
- We will need short-term partner success coverage during the staged rollout window — can your team assign an SE for the first two weeks of canary?
- On the commercial side, our procurement team will request a short SOW amendment that covers the engineering effort for the adapter. We’ll share a draft via DocuSign before the call.

Thanks — Tom and I will review the initial-rollforward-outline and come prepared with the customer matrix and a prioritized list of SDK versions. Looking forward to the demo.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Integrations
Aegis Tools
